items.title: For a zeta-stable module either it is the simple module concentrated at a vertex or the two maps of the complex are injective and surjective
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the dichotomy for a zeta-stable module at a vertex of the subgraph I^0 (author Lemma at source lines 1710-1720, label lem:betasurj): either the module is the simple module concentrated at that vertex, or the two maps of the complex are injective and surjective respectively. The proof (source lines 1724-1732) is a standard-argument one but with a real mechanism: it reads the kernel of alpha_i as a homomorphism from the simple module S_i to the stable module and then uses that both are zeta^bullet-stable with the same theta-functional value to conclude that a non-zero such homomorphism is an isomorphism (proof lines 1728-1731), and it obtains the surjectivity of beta_i by identifying its cokernel with the dual of the space of homomorphisms in the other direction (proof lines 1731-1732). The lemma is the technical input for the author's description of the strata, and the author notes just before the proof that it completes the proof of the preceding proposition. H2.
